target_customer: Canadian provincial health plans (fee-for-service billing) paying for physician-led programs for adults with type 2 diabetes and related conditions; later a US program
problem: Type 2 diabetes is usually managed with medication, while lifestyle change that can drive remission gets little physician time or reimbursement.
business_model: Fee-for-service billing of provincial health insurance (MSP, Alberta Health, OHIP) for physician visits, plus optional private-insurance add-ons
product_category: Virtual lifestyle medicine clinic for diabetes reversal

founders.name: Jason Kerkvliet
education: Princeton (described as a graduate on the YC page)
previous_startups: Described on the YC page as a recovering EMR founder; company not named
founders.background_notes: Directory sites list his title differently; YC page used.

founders.background_notes: Lifestyle medicine physician per YC page.

competitors.name: Virta Health
competitors.what: US virtual clinic for type 2 diabetes reversal using carbohydrate-restricted nutrition and remote monitoring
competitors.traction_then: Reversal program launched 2017; added prediabetes and obesity programs in 2020
competitors.funding_then: Raised large venture rounds by 2020 (a $133M round was reported)

technical_complexity.rationale: Telehealth scheduling, group sessions and billing; the founders had built EMR software before. The hard parts were clinical protocols and provincial billing rather than engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Provincial billing integration and a physician network help, but the clinical model is copyable by other clinics.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of an incumbent copying or buying the company as of 2026.

market_need_then: The YC page cites over 100M Americans with prediabetes or type 2 diabetes and $237B in yearly direct costs (company-reported); in Canada the model relies on existing public insurance coverage.

branding.domain_note: Company site is lifestylerx.io; a separate lifestylerx.com runs a US program page per search results.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain clinical language, 'proudly Canadian', $0 out of pocket framing

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community coverage of the brand itself found; name resembles other Rx lifestyle brands such as LifeRx.md that appeared in the same searches.

outcome_analysis: The company remains active as of 2026 with a 12-week physician-led program covered by provincial plans in BC, Alberta and Ontario, so it has not shown a shutdown. Its edge is reimbursement through public insurance rather than patient pay. Funding is only visible through aggregators, so growth trajectory beyond the YC batch is not public, and no later round could be confirmed.
notes: Aggregators (Tracxn via search, VCBacked) show a $500K pre-seed from Y Combinator dated 2023-09 and list Eight Capital as an investor; only aggregator sources, so unverified and not recorded as a round. One directory names different founder titles. Company claims of 2,000 patients and 46 percent reaching remission-range A1C are unverified. Update: the 500K pre-seed of September 2023 is recorded from VCBacked, with BounceWatch agreeing on amount and date (Y Combinator only); database basis only. Seedtable gives a last funding date of June 2023.
